expl: Madhya Pradesh currently shares border with five states namely Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra. Hence option (a) is wrong. stem: Which of the following was the capital of Andhra State when it was made a separate state in the year 1953?
expl: In an effort to gain a separate state based on linguistic grounds, Potti Shriramulu fasted until death in 1952. After Shriramulu's death, the Telugu speaking areas of Andhra state were carved out of Madras state in October, 1953 with Kurnool as its capital city. Later in 1956, Hyderabad was made the capital of Andhra Pradesh. Andhra Pradesh was bifurcated in 2014 and a separate state of Telangana was formed. However, in accordance with the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 Hyderabad will remain the de jure capital of both Andhra Pradesh and Telangana for a period not exceeding 10 years. The de facto capital city of Andhra Pradesh is Amaravati.

If the Yaman region of Pondicherry (now Puducherry) is also taken into consideration the number of States/Union Territories bordering Andhra Pradesh will be six. Tamil Nadu shares border with three states-Kerala, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh and including Pondicherry (now Puducherry), the number of States/Union Territories will be four. Telangana borders with Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. Thus, presently, Karnataka shares a border with the maximum number of states.
